text: Knowledge (intellect) is the cause of all worldly activity. It is of two kinds: memory and experience. Knowledge arising solely from impressions is memory. Knowledge distinct from that is experience. Experience is of two kinds: accurate and inaccurate. When the object exists, the experience of that nature is accurate; for example, the knowledge "this is silver" [when silver is present]. This is called valid knowledge. In the absence of the object, the experience of that nature is inaccurate; for example, the knowledge "this is silver" [when it is a pearl]. This is called invalid knowledge.
